 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.4036/2024 seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Sri.Devaraj Balasaheb Kumbhar S/o Balasaheb Kimayya Kumbhar, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 28.04.2024 at about 02.15 p.m, the deceased Devaraj Balasaheb Kumbhar was travelling in Lorry bearing No.MH-14-CP-5582 near Tavarekiere Bridge, Sira to Hiriyur Road, Tavarekere Village, Sira Taluk and he was driving the lorry at the left side of the road, at that time the driver of Lorry bearing No. KA-05-AE-2192 which was wrongly, carelessly and rash and negligently driven by its driver and caused the accident.
Due to impact, the deceased Devaraj Balasaheb Kumbhar who was the driver of the Lorry bearing No.MH-14-CP-558 sustained grievous injuries and died at the place of accident.
The petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation, travelling and funeral expenses.
Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 33 years and was working as Lorry Driver and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
The petitioners were entirely depending upon the earnings of the deceased.
On account of untimely death of the deceased, the (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.4036/2024 petitioners are put to great mental shock and agony, which cannot be compensated by any means.

The petitioner No.1 being wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 being minor children and petitioners No.4 and 5 being the parents of the deceased have lost love and affection, inspiration and financial support.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of above said offending lorry by its driver and in this regard the Tavarekere Police have registered a case against driver of said offending lorry.

The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence, it was placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and admits that this respondent issued a GCV Public Carrier other than 3 wheeler package policy bearing No.0704033123P106260074 in favour of the respondent No.1 in respect of Bharat Benz bearing No. (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.4036/2024 KA-05-AE-2192 and it is valid from 04.09.2023 to 03.09.2024 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is strictly in terms and conditions,
exceptions, limits and endorsement of the policy and further denied age, occupation, income of deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and dependency of the petitioners and manner of accident and involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.

The respondent No.1 had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident, thereby, there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy and also violation of Sec.150(2) of M.V. Act, hence, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.

The alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the deceased who was main architect for causing the alleged accident and there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the insured lorry.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant.

Hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against the respondent No.2.
05.
On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following Issues:-
(SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.4036/2024  ISSUES 01.

03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?

the respondent No.2 has not lead evidence, hence, respondent No.2 evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.
07. The counsels for the petitioners and respondent No.2 argued on the main matter and perused the records.

10. The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.5 is examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments.
Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing has been brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.

During the cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he denied to the suggestion that the accident is occurred due to negligence of deceased and not due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending lorry and (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.4036/2024 further admits that he has not produced any documents to show that his son was earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.

sentences.text: Accordingly, Issues No.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Devaraj Balasaheb Kumbhar, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.5 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 33 years and was working as Lorry Driver and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and they were entirely depending upon the earnings of the deceased
and they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation, travelling and funeral expenses.
On account of untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great mental shock and agony and they have lost love and affection, inspiration and financial support.
14. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.15 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied upon and according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 03.06.1991.
The alleged accident occurred on 28.04.2024 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 33 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased is (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.4036/2024 33 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 31 to 35 years is 16.
15.

sentences.text: So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioners have not produced any evidence or documents regarding avocation and income of the deceased.

Hence, in the absence of satisficatory evidence regarding avocation and income, this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru and as per norms for the year 2024 the notional income is Rs.16,500/- p.m and hence, this tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.16,500/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
16.

sentences.text: In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the minor children and petitioners No.4 and 5 are the parents of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

Therefore, considering the materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that there are five dependents and 1/4th of the (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.4036/2024 income of the deceased should be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

17. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

. Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.35,77,400/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Regarding liability:- Despite service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.

Though the respondent No.2 Insurance Company has appeared and filed written statement,
but not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioners.

Further, the respondent No.2 Insurance Company in its written statement at para 3 admits issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending Lorry and the same is valid from 04.09.2023 to 03.09.2024.
The alleged accident occurred on 28.04.2024.
Therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force.
The respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence or placed any material to show that the owner or driver of the offending lorry has violated terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.35,77,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a to the petitioners from the date of filing of the petition till (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.4036/2024 the date of deposit.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.4:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.35,77,400/- (Rupees Thirty five lakhs seventy seven thousand and four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 being children and petitioners No.4 and 5 are parents of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 40-20-20-10-10, in the award amount together with interest.

The petitioners No.1, 4 and 5 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award amount through (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.4036/2024 E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept Tanuja Devaraj Kumbhar vs Nanda Feeds Pvt Ltd on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76762621/

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 31 to 35 years is 16.
15.
So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioners have not produced any evidence or documents regarding avocation and income of the deceased.
Therefore, considering the materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that there are five dependents and 1/4th of the (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.4036/2024 income of the deceased should be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
18. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.4036/2024 Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.
Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
The respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence or placed any material to show that the owner or driver of the offending lorry has violated terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
